cleanIntro: This guide follows JK Armament's 195, 155 & 105 Series Operation and Maintenance Manual (issued September 2022). The book gives the 195 VERSAX 12GA its own section and calls it the little brother to the longer 195 SGX 12GA: it ships as a taper mount, a tube, four SGX baffle assemblies and a cylinder choke end cap. The maintenance JK publishes is one short procedure for every suppressor in the book: off the gun and cool, unthread each component, clean every part with ammonia-free CLP and a nylon brush, inspect every part and thread, then put a light coat of CLP on the threads and thread it back together hand-tight. The book goes no further than that.

steps.title: Shotgun unloaded, action open, before the can comes off
steps.action: Keep the host shotgun pointed in a safe direction. Unload it and open the action so you can see it is clear of ammunition, following that shotgun's own manual. Only then reach for the suppressor.
steps.prose: The suppressor has no action of its own to clear. JK's book covers the can; unloading the gun belongs to the gun's own manual.
steps.quote: Before removing the suppressor from the host firearm, be sure the firearm is unloaded and the action is opened so it is visibly clear of any ammunition.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (printed on PDF p.1); the hand-download file is named '2025' — 2.0 Installation, PDF p.3
steps.warn: Before removing the suppressor from the host firearm, be sure the firearm is unloaded and the action is opened so it is visibly clear of any ammunition.

steps.title: Let it cool, or wear heat-resistant gloves
steps.action: Assume the suppressor is hot if it has been fired. Let it cool, or put on heat-resistant gloves before you grip it.
steps.prose: JK rates the VERSAX 12GA for full-auto bursts, and a can that has just been shot looks the same as a cold one.
steps.quote: When removing the suppressor, use extreme caution as it may be hot to the touch after firing. Use heat-resistant gloves to avoid burns or other injuries.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (printed on PDF p.1); the hand-download file is named '2025' — 2.0 Installation, PDF p.3
steps.warn: When removing the suppressor, use extreme caution as it may be hot to the touch after firing. Use heat-resistant gloves to avoid burns or other injuries.

steps.title: Off the muzzle, and a thread protector on the barrel
steps.action: Take the suppressor off the host shotgun. Once it is off, put a thread protector or another muzzle device on the barrel so the threads and crown are covered while the gun is stored or carried.
steps.prose: The book gives no step-by-step for taking the can off the muzzle, and it prints no mount thread for the 195 system. What it does say is to protect the bare threads once the can is off.
steps.quote: Once the suppressor is removed from the host firearm, JK Armament recommends using a thread protector or other muzzle device to protect the muzzle threads and crown during storage or transport.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (printed on PDF p.1); the hand-download file is named '2025' — 2.0 Installation, PDF p.3

steps.title: Unthread each component
steps.action: Unthread the suppressor's components from one another. If a joint will not turn by hand, a crescent or combination wrench may be used. Keep the four baffle assemblies in order as they come out so they go back the same way.
steps.prose: The wrenches JK names by series are its 155 and 105 wrenches; the book names no 195 series wrench. The book does not say whether the taper mount comes off its tube, so this guide does not tell you to force it. If a joint was assembled with removable thread locker, it may need heat before it will break loose.
steps.quote: Unthread each component. Use a JK 155 or JK 105 series wrench to disassemble, if necessary. A crescent wrench or a combination wrench may also be used.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (printed on PDF p.1); the hand-download file is named '2025' — 4.0 Maintenance, Disassembly, PDF p.25
steps.warn: If Blue Loctite® or other removable thread locker was used, the unit may need to be heated prior to disassembly.

steps.title: Field strip complete: every component unthreaded
steps.action: The suppressor is off the gun and every component is unthreaded. That is all the disassembly JK's book describes. The cleaning, inspection and reassembly JK publishes are in Deep Clean, at the end of the clean steps.
steps.prose: Everything JK asks you to clean is a component, a thread or a face. The book gives no deeper procedure than unthreading the parts.
steps.quote: From tactical operations to sporting clays to bird hunting, there has never been a more capable shotgun suppressor than the JK 195 VERSAX 12GA.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (printed on PDF p.1); the hand-download file is named '2025' — 3.11 JK 195 VERSAX 12GA, PDF p.17

deepSteps.title: Clean every component with ammonia-free CLP and a nylon brush
deepSteps.action: Scrub every component with an ammonia-free CLP and a nylon brush. Work somewhere you can contain the residue, wash your hands afterwards, and dispose of the dirty patches and solvent properly.
deepSteps.prose: JK names both the cleaner and the brush. The fouling inside a suppressor can carry lead and other toxic material, so treat what comes off the parts accordingly.
deepSteps.quote: Clean all components with an appropriate CLP (ammonia free) and a nylon brush.
deepSteps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (printed on PDF p.1); the hand-download file is named '2025' — 4.0 Maintenance, Disassembly, PDF p.25
deepSteps.warn: Lead and other toxic materials may be deposited inside of your suppressor; use appropriate cautions and disposal methods when cleaning.

deepSteps.title: Get the carbon off every thread and face
deepSteps.action: Pay particular attention to the threads and the mating faces of each component. Brush the carbon off them until the threads are clean and the faces are bare.
deepSteps.prose: Carbon left on a thread or a face stops the parts seating squarely when they are threaded back together.
deepSteps.quote: Keep carbon deposits off of threads and faces of all components.
deepSteps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (printed on PDF p.1); the hand-download file is named '2025' — 4.0 Maintenance, PDF p.25

deepSteps.title: Inspect every component and thread
deepSteps.action: Look over every component and every thread for damage before anything goes back together.
deepSteps.prose: JK asks for this inspection after cleaning and again before assembling.
deepSteps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (printed on PDF p.1); the hand-download file is named '2025' — 4.0 Maintenance, Disassembly, PDF p.25

deepSteps.title: Light coat of CLP on the threads
deepSteps.action: Before assembling, put a light coat of CLP on the threads, and look the components and threads over once more.
deepSteps.prose: A light coat is what JK asks for, on the threads.
deepSteps.quote: Before assembling, apply a light coat of CLP to threads and inspect all components and threads.
deepSteps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (printed on PDF p.1); the hand-download file is named '2025' — 4.0 Maintenance, Assembly, PDF p.25

deepSteps.title: Thread it back together, hand-tight, without cross-threading
deepSteps.action: Thread the components back together in the order they came apart. Start each thread carefully so it does not cross-thread, and tighten by hand.
deepSteps.prose: A cross-threaded joint can damage both parts, so if a thread will not start smoothly, back it out and start it again.
deepSteps.quote: Thread together the connections, taking care not to cross thread. Hand tighten the components together.
deepSteps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (printed on PDF p.1); the hand-download file is named '2025' — 4.0 Maintenance, Assembly, PDF p.25

deepSteps.title: If you torque it: 10 ft/lbs at most
deepSteps.action: If you want to set a torque rather than hand-tighten, do not go past 10 ft/lbs. One drop of Blue 242 Loctite® can be used if you want the assembly to hold more firmly.
deepSteps.prose: If you use thread locker, remember the disassembly caution: next time, that joint may need heat before it will come apart.
deepSteps.quote: If a torque setting is desired, do not exceed 10 ft/lbs. One drop of Blue 242 Loctite® can be used for a more robust configuration.
deepSteps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (printed on PDF p.1); the hand-download file is named '2025' — 4.0 Maintenance, Assembly, PDF p.25

cleaning.name: OFF THE GUN, COOL
tasks: Host shotgun unloaded, action open, visibly clear of ammunition
Suppressor cool, or heat-resistant gloves on
Thread protector or muzzle device on the bare muzzle threads

cleaning.name: UNTHREAD
tasks: Each component unthreaded, by hand or with a crescent or combination wrench
The four baffle assemblies kept in order so they go back the same way
⚠ Joints assembled with removable thread locker may need heat first

cleaning.name: CLEAN AND INSPECT
tasks: Every component scrubbed with ammonia-free CLP and a nylon brush
Carbon off every thread and face
⚠ Fouling may carry lead and other toxic material: contain it and dispose of it properly

cleaning.name: ASSEMBLE
tasks: Light coat of CLP on the threads
If torqued, no more than 10 ft/lbs; one drop of Blue 242 Loctite® optional

cleaning.name: LEAVE ALONE
tasks: ⛔ Never use a crush washer when mounting the suppressor
⛔ Never shoot through an obstructed suppressor
Do not exceed 10 ft/lbs on any connection
⚠ JK presently does not recommend high-density shot such as Hevi-Shot, Federal TSS, tungsten or bismuth

reassembly: Every component cleaned, inspected, lightly coated with CLP on the threads and threaded back together hand-tight in the order it came apart, without cross-threading, and no more than 10 ft/lbs if torqued.
Host shotgun unloaded with the action open before the suppressor goes back on.
The suppressor checked free of obstructions such as mud or dirt; if it has been in water, left to drain completely.
Mounted with no crush washer, fully shouldered on the barrel with no visible gap between the barrel shoulder and the face of the thread mount or muzzle device.
fncheck: With the host shotgun unloaded and the action open: check the fit between barrel and suppressor before firing. The mount must be fully shouldered, with no visible gap between the barrel shoulder and the face of the thread mount or muzzle device, and no crush washer anywhere in the stack. Check the suppressor is free of obstructions. Once shooting, JK recommends checking that the suppressor is still tight after 30 rounds, and it may be hot when you do.
